prompt: A computer supplies web pages to other computers on the network. What role does it perform?
options: It performs a transit role because several clients use it.
It performs a client role while returning the requested pages.
It performs a switching role when it receives Ethernet frames.
It performs a server role while remaining a network endpoint.
explanation: A server supplies a service such as HTTP to clients, and it is still an endpoint. The two roles do not exclude each other.

whyWrong.0: Supplying an application is not forwarding other hosts’ traffic in a transit role.
whyWrong.1: It supplies the web content; a client requests it.
whyWrong.2: Receiving its own frames is not switching frames between ports.

prompt: A PC must send an IP packet to a different IP network. Which function selects the next hop from the destination IP address?
options: A Layer 2 switch forwarding within one VLAN
An access point accepting a wireless association
A router consulting its IP routing table
A hub repeating the received electrical signal
explanation: Routing picks the outgoing path from the destination IP network using the routing table. A router, or a Layer 3 switch with routing enabled, does this.

whyWrong.0: Layer 2 forwarding uses MAC addresses within one VLAN and selects no IP next hop.
whyWrong.1: Wireless association joins a client to an AP and does not choose routes between IP networks.
whyWrong.3: A hub repeats signals and has no routing table.

prompt: A company wants a consistent wireless configuration across many access points. What is the main role of a wireless LAN controller?
options: Coordinate the configuration and operation of supported APs.
Provide each wireless client’s physical radio attachment itself.
Supply power allocation independently of the AP’s PoE switch.
Choose every client’s IP next hop as the campus core.
explanation: A wireless LAN controller centrally configures and monitors the access points it manages. The data-forwarding path depends on the deployment.

whyWrong.1: The AP, not the controller, provides the client’s radio attachment.
whyWrong.2: Power comes from the PoE switch port, not the controller.
whyWrong.3: A controller coordinates APs; routing is a separate function.

prompt: What is the main purpose of the core in a three-tier campus design?
options: Connect individual users and APs to the campus.
Provide transport between distribution blocks.
Combine the roles of distribution and access.
Connect each leaf to every other leaf directly.
explanation: The core interconnects distribution blocks and carries traffic between them. Access layers attach endpoints, and distribution aggregates access switches.

whyWrong.0: Attaching users and APs is the access layer’s job.
whyWrong.2: A separate core is not a combined access and distribution layer.
whyWrong.3: Leaf-to-leaf links belong to spine-leaf, not a three-tier core.

prompt: A hosted application automatically adds capacity as demand grows and releases it when demand falls. Which cloud characteristic does this illustrate?
options: Rapid elasticity
Resource pooling
Broad network access
Measured service
explanation: Rapid elasticity is expanding and releasing provisioned capacity as demand changes. Hosting a server in someone else’s building is not elasticity.

whyWrong.1: Resource pooling means shared provider resources, not capacity changing with demand.
whyWrong.2: Broad network access describes how the service is reached.

prompt: Which two statements accurately describe a next-generation firewall and an inline IPS? (Choose two.)
options: An NGFW can apply policy using identified applications.
An inline IPS can drop traffic according to its threat policy.
A stateful firewall uses only the destination IP, ignoring connection state.
An inline IPS inspects only an out-of-path traffic copy.
An NGFW’s encrypted-payload visibility is independent of decryption.
explanation: An NGFW enforces policy using identified applications, and an inline IPS sits in the traffic path and can drop traffic that matches its threat policy.

whyWrong.2: A stateful firewall tracks connection state, not only the destination IP.
whyWrong.3: An inline IPS sits in the traffic path; inspecting an out-of-path copy is passive monitoring.
whyWrong.4: Seeing inside encrypted payloads requires decryption, whatever the NGFW can do.

exhibit.title: Documented forwarding behavior — teaching evidence, not CLI output
exhibit.text:
SW3 forwards frames between local ports in each VLAN.
SW3 is configured with IP routing and serves as gateway for two IP networks.
Traffic between those networks is routed by SW3.

prompt: Which device role matches the documented behavior of SW3?
options: A Layer 2 switch providing management access
A wireless controller managing radio settings
A hub connecting a shared Ethernet segment
A Layer 3 switch performing routing and switching
explanation: SW3 forwards Ethernet frames within each LAN and routes between IP networks, which is a Layer 3 switch.

whyWrong.0: A Layer 2 switch with a management address does not route between networks.
whyWrong.1: The evidence shows wired switching and routing, not AP management.
whyWrong.2: A hub does not learn MAC addresses or make IP routing decisions.

prompt: An office adds compatible controller-managed access points on PoE switch ports. Which two statements describe the design correctly? (Choose two.)
options: The AP uses its wired uplink only for power, with no Ethernet data.
The AP connects wireless clients to the wired network through its uplink.
The controller’s budget replaces the switch’s PoE power budget.
The switch can supply power and Ethernet connectivity on the AP’s cable.
Controller management means client forwarding always bypasses the AP’s site.
explanation: The AP connects wireless clients to the wired network, and a compatible PoE switch supplies both Ethernet and power on the same cable. The controller manages the AP but does not replace the switch’s power budget.

whyWrong.0: The uplink carries Ethernet data as well as power.
whyWrong.2: The switch’s own PoE budget limits the power it can supply.
whyWrong.4: Management and forwarding are separate; some designs switch client traffic locally at the AP.

exhibit.title: Campus design notes
exhibit.text:
Access switches connect users and APs.
Their uplinks reach a redundant pair of switches.
That pair performs both distribution and core functions.
There is no separate core layer.

prompt: Which campus architecture matches the exhibit?
options: A two-tier campus with a collapsed distribution/core layer
A three-tier campus because the upper layer has two switches
A spine-leaf fabric because every access switch has two uplinks
A single access layer because all switches share one site
explanation: Combined distribution and core functions above the access layer make a two-tier design with a collapsed core. Redundant switches in one layer do not add a tier.

whyWrong.1: Tiers count functional layers, not the number of switches.
whyWrong.2: Two uplinks per access switch do not make a spine-leaf fabric.
whyWrong.3: The exhibit shows access plus a combined distribution/core layer, not a single layer.

exhibit.title: Basic spine-leaf plan
exhibit.text:
Spines: S1, S2
Leaves: L1, L2, L3
Each leaf connects to S1 and S2.
Servers attach to leaf ports.

prompt: Which two additions fit the basic spine-leaf connection pattern in the plan? Choose two.
options: Add L4 with one link to S1 and one to S2.
Connect a new server to S1 instead of a leaf.
Attach a new server to an available L2 port.
Connect L4 only to L3, using L3 as its transit leaf.
Replace L2’s two spine links with one L1–L2 link.
explanation: In basic spine-leaf, each leaf connects to every spine and servers attach only to leaves. A new leaf needs a link to both spines, and a new server goes on a leaf port.

whyWrong.1: Servers attach to leaves, not spines.
whyWrong.3: A leaf must connect to every spine, not depend on another leaf.
whyWrong.4: A leaf-to-leaf link replaces the required spine connections and breaks the pattern.

exhibit.title: PoE allocation worksheet — supplied values
exhibit.text:
Available budget: 120 W
Existing allocations: 90 W
Remaining budget: 30 W
Each proposed AP allocation: 30 W

prompt: Each additional AP needs a 30 W allocation, and each selected port supports it. Based on the stated total budget, how many more such APs can the switch support?
options: Three additional APs
Two additional APs
No additional APs
One additional AP
explanation: The remaining budget is 120 − 90 = 30 W, which covers one more 30 W AP. Both the per-port limit and the total budget must allow it.

whyWrong.0: Three APs would need 90 W more than is left.
whyWrong.1: Two APs would need 60 W, more than the 30 W remaining.
whyWrong.2: The remaining 30 W covers one 30 W AP.

prompt: On a home device that combines routing, switching and an AP, wired clients reach the Internet but wireless clients cannot see the network name. Which function do you check first?
options: The WAN routing function that the wired clients are using
The wireless access-point function and its radio configuration
The Ethernet switching function serving the wired clients
The remote Internet server used by both kinds of client
explanation: Wired clients work, so routing and switching are fine. The failure is wireless discovery, which points to the AP’s radio and SSID settings.

whyWrong.0: Working wired Internet access shows the WAN path is up.
whyWrong.2: The wired clients’ Ethernet attachment is working.
whyWrong.3: Clients must join the wireless network before they can reach any remote server.

prompt: Three branches reach each other only through headquarters over separate WAN links. What happens if HQ’s transit function fails?
options: Branch-A loses local switching as well as its WAN path.
The branches retain communication through their local gateways alone.
Communication between branches loses its only designed path.
Only requests addressed to HQ itself are affected.
explanation: In hub-and-spoke, branch-to-branch traffic depends on the hub. If the hub fails, that path is lost while each branch LAN keeps working.

whyWrong.0: An HQ failure does not stop switching inside Branch-A.
whyWrong.1: Local gateways give no other path between branches.
whyWrong.3: Traffic that merely passes through HQ is affected too.

exhibit.title: Office test record — supplied evidence
exhibit.text:
PC-A and Server-A: same local subnet, different addresses
PC-A → Server-A ping: replies received
PC-A → Server-A new HTTP request: no service response
Server-A Services → HTTP: Off

prompt: Which change fixes the confirmed cause without disturbing the working path?
options: Assign a management IP address to the switch.
Enable HTTP on Server-A, then repeat the fresh request.
Give PC-A a default gateway for this local destination.
Move Server-A to a different subnet before testing.
explanation: The server setting shows HTTP is stopped, and ping already works. Enable HTTP on Server-A and repeat the request.

whyWrong.0: A working ping shows local switching needs no switch management address.
whyWrong.2: The server is in the client’s own subnet, so no default gateway is needed.
whyWrong.3: Changing the subnet does not start the stopped service.

prompt: In Power over Ethernet, what is the power sourcing equipment (PSE)?
options: The switch or injector that supplies power
The phone or AP that receives power
The cable that carries the data
The controller that manages the AP
explanation: The PSE is the PoE-capable switch or injector that supplies power. The device receiving it is the powered device (PD).

whyWrong.1: The device receiving power is the powered device (PD).
whyWrong.2: The cable carries power and data; it is not the PSE.
whyWrong.3: A controller coordinates APs and does not supply power.

prompt: What is the maximum power an 802.3at (PoE+, Type 2) port supplies at the PSE?
explanation: 802.3at supplies up to 30 W at the PSE port.

prompt: Which cloud service model supplies virtual machines, storage and networks on which the customer runs its own operating systems and applications?
options: SaaS
PaaS
IaaS
DaaS
explanation: IaaS (infrastructure as a service) supplies virtual machines, storage and networks for the customer’s own operating systems and applications.

whyWrong.1: PaaS supplies a managed platform for the customer’s application code.
whyWrong.3: DaaS is not one of the three service models in this chapter.

prompt: In a basic spine-leaf design, which statement is true?
options: Every leaf connects to every spine
Leaves connect to each other
Servers attach directly to spines
Spines connect to each other
explanation: In basic spine-leaf, every leaf connects to every spine and servers attach only to leaves. Leaves do not connect to leaves, and spines do not connect to spines.

whyWrong.1: Leaves do not connect to other leaves.
whyWrong.3: Spines do not connect to other spines.
